subject: Pioneer4B: Intermittent 503s and fallback behavior
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme-corp.com>, Tim Fowler <tim.fowler@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jul 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pioneer4B: Intermittent 503s and fallback behavior

Hi Laura / Tim,

Short heads-up: between ~07:45 and 09:10 PT this morning we saw an increase in 5xx/timeout responses for requests routed to the Pioneer4B model for your account. Our serving runtime detected elevated token-step failures and automatically routed a portion of requests to a smaller fallback model; you may have observed higher latencies and some truncated responses while that routing was active.

What we know so far:
- Window: ~07:45 - 09:10 PT (spike peaked ~08:05)
- Affected surface: generate endpoint using Pioneer4B (ctx lengths > 2k tokens saw higher failure rate)
- Observable behavior: 503 responses, some timeouts at edge, and higher median latency for failing requests that then retried to fallback model

Immediate actions taken by Redwood:
- Triggered automated fallback population to the fallback pool (smaller model) to preserve availability
- Opened PagerDuty incident RWI-789334 and routed ops to triage
- Collected request ids and sample payloads (attached: pioneer4b-error-samples.txt)

Could you confirm if you observed customer-facing errors beyond what automated retries handled (e.g., user-facing failures, lost work) and share any request ids you have for impacted calls? We want to prioritize any follow-ups for your team.

We’ll follow up with a technical update shortly. Apologies for the interruption — we’re treating this as high priority.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Lead, Enterprise Success
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pioneer4b-error-samples.txt (text/plain)]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 21 Jul 2028 10:40:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Pioneer4B: Intermittent 503s and fallback behavior

Karthik — forwarding initial note and a quick triage summary.

On Fri, Jul 21, 2028 at 08:12 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Laura / Tim,
> 
> Short heads-up: between ~07:45 and 09:10 PT this morning we saw an increase in 5xx/timeout responses for requests routed to the Pioneer4B model for your account.

Triage notes (ops):
- Reproduced locally against a sampled request: observe kernel-level slowdowns in the quantized attention path when ctx > ~2048 tokens under high concurrent KV-cache pressure.
- Evidence: repeated L2 cache misses on the NVLink path and sporadic memory pressure leading to a per-process watchdog-triggered termination that manifests as 503 upstream. See attached trace snippets.
- Fallbacks behaved as designed; we measured ~92% of traffic successfully served by fallback model after automatic routing kicked in.

Planned remediation steps (next 48 hrs):
1) Backport urgent kernel guard to mitigate the watchdog-triggered terminations (hotfix rolling tonight, 23:00 PT).
2) Adjust routing policy thresholds for Pioneer4B to be more aggressive on ctx length until the kernel update is in production.
3) Add an additional KV-cache capacity shard for Pioneer4B pools to reduce per-host pressure (follow-up change, targeted next week).

Attachments: pioneer4b-kernel-trace-snippets.log

I’ll coordinate the roll and update once the hotfix lands.

—Marissa
Senior SRE, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference

Can you confirm whether this will be counted toward our SLA for July? Also — appreciate the hotfix window; please keep us posted on timing for the kernel patch and any expected rolling restarts.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme-corp.com>, Tim Fowler <tim.fowler@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 23 Jul 2028 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Pioneer4B: Recovery confirmed and next steps (postmortem draft)

Hi Laura / Tim — final update and commitments after our patch window.

Summary of resolution:
- Root cause: under high concurrency and long-context sequences, a combination of NVLink L2 cache thrashing and a latent race in the quantized attention kernel could trigger a per-process watchdog which caused the serving process to exit and surface 5xx upstream.
- Mitigation applied 23 Jul 23:00 PT: hotfix guard introduced to the kernel attention path + aggressive routing threshold for Pioneer4B (ctx > 1.5k immediately routed to fallback).
- Outcome: after the hotfix and routing adjustment, error rate for Pioneer4B dropped to baseline (<0.01% 5xx) and automated fallbacks reduced end-user impact. We validated with a synthetic concurrency test and with your sampled request ids.

Attachments and artifacts:
- pioneer4b-kernel-trace-snippets.log (ops traces)
- pioneer4b-error-samples.txt (customer request ids & payload stubs)
- pioneer4b-postmortem-draft.pdf (we’ve included the draft postmortem and planned timeline for the permanent fix)

Action items & commitments:
1) Permanent fix (kernel rework + extended KV-cache sharding) targeted for 2028-08-07 deployment window (engineering change request RW-POST-1245).
2) Configuration change: we will keep the aggressive routing threshold for Pioneer4B until the permanent fix is validated in canary (expected 2 weeks).
3) Credits: We’re investigating SLA exposure for the spike; if this meets SLA credit criteria we’ll apply a service credit to your July invoice (I’ll confirm by EOD Tue).
4) Postmortem review: invite to a review meeting the week of 2028-07-29 — I’ll send a calendar invite and the finalized postmortem prior to the meeting.

If you have additional request ids or a short list of user-impact examples, please send them and we’ll include them in the root-cause appendix. Apologies again for the incident and thanks for the patience — happy to hop on a call if helpful.

Best regards,
Karthik Iyer
Account Lead, Enterprise Success
Redwood Inference
